title: paged KV cache: block allocator reuse and pinning optimizations (v2)
author: Morgan Blake
description: Motivation: reduce KV cache fragmentation and allocator churn under mixed-length workloads, and improve tail latency for streaming generation by keeping hot KV blocks pinned when eviction pressure is transient. This PR extends the paged KV cache block manager with a reuse-first allocation path, conservative pinning heuristics, and a small TTL-based recency bypass to prefer recently-used allocations for short-lived requests. The change set touches allocator internals, eviction logic, and exposes two tuning knobs (reuse_window_ms, pin_reservation_limit) with sensible defaults. Summary of changes: - Implemented fast-path that attempts to reuse recently freed blocks matching size class before falling back to slow allocator. - Added pin reservation table with soft limits to avoid thrashing during bursty traffic. - TTL-based recency: blocks freed within reuse_window_ms are preferred for reuse; fallback still guarantees correctness. - Updated metrics (kv.block_reuse_hits, kv.block_pin_failures, kv.allocator_pressure) and added a perf bench harness to reproduce mixed-length burst scenarios. Testing & CI: included unit tests for allocator correctness, property tests for pin/unpin invariants, integration bench that runs on perf-canary CI job. Performance summary: on internal bench with mixed-length chat workload we see 18-23% reduction in median per-request CPU for KV operations and up to 11% improvement in P95 tail for streaming completion under 90th-percentile load. Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration bench, [x] docs snippet, [x] add metrics and traces, [x] runtime flag gating for canary rollout. Related: ENG-4123, ENG-4276. Notes: this is a conservative v2 iteration after initial feedback (see review comments) to reduce pin reservation pressure and tighten reuse matching rules.

review_comments: Lena Cho (reviewer): The reuse fast-path looks promising, but I worry about fragmentation for variable-size allocations. Can we add a size-class fallback and a max-reuse-age to avoid long-term cross-contamination?
Morgan Blake (author): Agree, added size-class matching and reuse_window_ms to prefer recently-freed blocks only. See allocator.rs change set for matching rules.

Diego Alvarez (reviewer): Pin reservation semantics need to be conservative — during canary we saw reservation exhaustion on burst tests. Consider soft limits and metrics so ops teams can tune online.
Morgan Blake (author): Implemented pin_reservation_limit as a soft limit that returns pin failure but leaves block free for eviction; added kv.block_pin_failures metric and alert guidance in docs.
Priya Natarajan (reviewer): Please add a unit test asserting pin/unpin invariants and a small property test for concurrent pin attempts.
Morgan Blake (author): Added allocator_tests.rs with deterministic pin/unpin scenarios and a randomized property test that runs in CI.
Lena Cho (approver): LGTM after the pin reservation soft-limit and additional tests. Approving for merge.
Diego Alvarez (approver): Approve. Verified perf bench reproduces improvement on perf-canary cluster.
release_notes: Improves KV cache efficiency by reusing recently freed blocks and reducing allocator churn; adds conservative pinning to reduce eviction-induced tail latency. Includes new metrics for tuning.
summary_perf_results: Bench (mixed-length chat workload, perf-canary): KV CPU per-request median -18% (95% CI ±2%), P95 streaming latency -11% under sustained load; memory fragmentation reduced by ~9% on traced runs. Results are from bench/mixed_length_bench.rs with config: reuse_window_ms=250, pin_reservation_limit=32.
notes_for_ops: Default flags are conservative (reuse_window_ms=250ms, pin_reservation_limit=32). Recommend canary rollout to 5% traffic and watch kv.block_pin_failures and kv.allocator_pressure metrics before wider rollout. If pin failures spike, lower pin_reservation_limit or increase reuse_window_ms.
migration_instructions: No data migration required. New metrics will appear after deploy. To enable experimental aggressive reuse set runtime flag kv.reuse_enabled=true via runtime_flags.
